P01.note: The single sentence 'crossed into the neighboring parish, cut down the maypole ... and fought off the neighbors' hands over 'raid' on its own. 'Roundup' falls on a surface read because nothing is herded (the ponies are only scenery); 'pilgrimage' literally fits the walk to the boundary stone, and 'pageant' is the only near-miss that survives.

P02.note: 'Corridor' is the expected answer for a strip between two forests and is killed by 'settle ... within a few hundred yards of where they entered'; 'cage' is killed by voles that 'wander back'. 'Cafeteria' literally matches the 'seed-heavy grass', and only the owl-pellet sentence together with the equal survival at the forest edge moves it to 'cemetery'.

P03.note: Each distractor has its own planted denial: 'soil tests no richer' (fertilized), 'leaving no worn paths' (furrowed), and turf 'an inch high, with tiny flowers' (denuded). 'Furrowed' also falls on a surface read because grazing sheep do not plow. Once those three are read, 'groomed' is just the option left over.

P04.note: The sieving sentence (boulders, then cobbles, then pea gravel) points to 'sorted'. Each wrong word is denied by one later sentence: 'lying wherever they stopped' (stacked), 'same shade inside as out' (stained), and 'broken pebbles still fit back together edge to edge' (sanded). That is a kill list, not inference.

P05.note: 'Half again as much oxygen as the bay' hands over 'lung' by itself. 'As brown with mud' and 'as much fertilizer nitrate' kill kidney and net directly. 'Kitchen' rests only on the fish crowding, and the passage ties that to oxygen, so it is weak.

P06.note: The key is literal: 'lined both banks with cut stone' is walling. 'Quick current' kills stilled, 'the whole stream ran past it' kills siphoned, and 'Trout below the mill were as many as above it' kills soured, one sentence for each.

P07.note: 'Old crumbling crust ... still there' kills both incised and milled. 'Littered' literally describes spreading stones and is the near-miss, ruled out only by 'forty feet deep from wall to wall' and the smooth floor, which make it a continuous cover rather than a scatter.

P08.note: 'Firebreak' is the planted trap; the reader has to work out from the layout that the river, not the north wall, stood between the orchard and the burning village. 'Dike' fails because the river is on the south edge, and 'fence' because the wall is 'open at both ends'. Frost-proof peaches and bricks 'warm to the hand at midnight' support 'hearth'.

P09.note: The ledger sentence (goods left 'against credit', 'redeemed', the rest sold each fall) defines a pawnshop outright. 'The bottles held whiskey' kills pharmacy and 'barred the door at sundown' kills parlor. 'Repository' literally fits the safe but misses the credit-and-redemption terms.

P10.note: 'Few lingering' and the empty benches kill magnet, and 'lawns slope open to the highway' kills muffler. 'Mixer' (two divided neighborhoods brought together) is the real near-miss; only the commuter flow of paths to the footbridge and station favours 'junction'.

P11.note: 'Depository' is suggested by the cool dry air and the war-storage setting, but it is killed by paintings hung 'uncrated' that townspeople 'walk past' every Sunday, which makes it a gallery. 'Stayed there unchanged' kills hospital and 'every one went back up' kills dump.

P12.note: 'Mummified' is the near-miss, because the hull 'looked as sound as on the day it sank', but planks crumbling 'into a lace of pencil-wide tunnels' make it 'mined'. 'Upright on the open bottom' kills interred and 'outline whole' kills jostled. The key is a stretch, since seawater itself does not tunnel.

P13.note: 'Water from just beneath the reservoir's sunlit surface' kills chilled and 'bars shift from week to week' kills clogged. The daily surge-and-trickle supports 'churned', but 'bled' (drained to 'a trickle between dry gravel bars' every night) is also defensible, and nothing in the passage separates the two.

P14.note: 'Only gnawed stumps remain' decides 'deforested' alone. The other three are each denied by one sentence: dams that 'washes out' (flooded), 'the same shallow, stony bed' (dredged) and 'both valleys turn the same brown' (greened). Popular beaver lore points the reader to 'greened', and the passage simply negates it.

P15.note: The sequence 'sprouted and then crushed' with 'three days' and an exactly doubled column is a recipe being scaled, and it all sits in one sentence. 'Roadmap' falls on a surface read because nothing on the tablet concerns a route, and 'payroll' has no names. 'Receipt' (amounts plus a seal) is the only live distractor.

P16.note: 'Grown over with corals and sponges along every beam' while the sand 'holds almost none' gives 'trellis'. 'Tripwire' is off topic on a surface read, since nothing in the passage is about a hazard to ships. 'All thirty of its crew rowed ashore' kills tomb, and coal cargo kills strongbox.

P17.note: 'Kept green needles' kills scorched and 'growth rings as wide as before' kills sapped. 'Tallest and soundest' seems planted against winnowed's culling-the-weak sense, but 'winnowed' as 'thinned' still fits one tree in five lost. 'Toppled the forest' overclaims for 20% and credits the gales' work to the dry years, so the pair is not separated.

P18.note: 'Herded' is the textbook ant-aphid trope and is killed by aphids that 'stayed on whatever shoot they had settled on, wilting or not'. 'Walked as quickly on leaves the workers had crossed' kills drugged, and 'the eggs hatched' kills devoured. Eggs carried down and heaped for winter make 'garnered'.

P19.note: Three short planted sentences each kill one option: 'stayed in private hands' (nationalized), 'No censor read their pages' (muzzled) and 'sales climbing' (impoverished). 'Mobilized' is what is left, and it is supported by the recruiting appeals.

P20.note: 'As many elk ... as ever' kills reduced, 'kept to their old ranges' kills redistributed, and 'grazed heads down as long as before' kills rattled, all in one sentence. Kills of old and lame elk plus more calves surviving support 'rejuvenated'.

P21.note: 'Moisture readings ... a third of those on the bare half' is the key stated literally. 'Stood firm in sound mortar' kills dislodged, 'stone faces under the stems were clean' kills etched, and the gale that 'left both halves standing' kills fortified.

P22.note: 'Patrolled' is the expected ant-plant mutualism and is killed by ants that stay in the thorns by day while caterpillars chew 'banded and unbanded shrubs alike'. 'Flowered and podded as heavily' kills pollinated, and 'seeds dropped beneath them as their neighbors' did' kills propagated. Banded shrubs 'grew a third taller', which makes 'parasitized'.

P23.note: 'On the same level ground' kills lifted, and 'Caravans kept reaching the eastern gate' kills imprisoned. 'Lashed' fails on the gradual 'few dozen yards' every decade and houses given up 'one at a time', which also builds 'nibbled'.

P24.note: One sentence, 'the council, over the objections of the church's trustees, moved ... into the nave', defines commandeered. 'Crated' falls on a surface read because a stone church cannot be crated. 'Walls sound' kills condemned and 'got their church back, unaltered' kills bulldozed, so no near-miss survives.

P25.note: 'Misspellings ... included' kills tidied, 'nothing in it comes from outside them' kills spliced, and 'Line by line ... down to the weekly egg tallies' kills tightened. The curse rendered as 'my husband was tired today' then supplies 'softened'.

P26.note: 'Kept the family's names, its fjord, its money' kills naturalized, the preserved 'short, abrupt rhythm' kills manicured, and 'a few lines' in 'a handful of scenes' makes mutilated too strong. Drownings turned into rescues give 'lightened'.

P27.note: 'Strewn over half a mile of open sand' gives 'dismantled'. 'Open sand' kills entombed, 'scoured smooth and pale' kills encrusted, and 'wood still heavy and sound' kills gnawed, one phrase each.

P28.note: 'With her name on the title page' kills plagiarized, the near-miss. 'Named two of the poems among the season's best' kills panned and 'barely four hundred copies' kills popularized. The reprint sentence alone, same poems at half price paying her nothing, defines pirated.

P29.note: 'Townspeople with coughs sent up by doctors for the dry air ... went home well' is the dictionary definition of a sanatorium. 'Vault' falls on a surface read because nothing in the passage is stored. 'Drovers ... sent on to the village inn' kills tavern and 'bought their prayer books from a printer' kills scriptorium.

P30.note: 'Banquet' (the whale-fall feast trope) is killed by 'the same few sleeper sharks', 'a mouthful or two' and 'no animal living on it'. 'Bridge' falls on a surface read because nothing crosses anything. 'Battery' (a store drawn down slowly) is a real near-miss to 'cupboard'.

P31.note: 'Canvas hanging from the yards, on water so still that scraps ... floated beside the hulls' is becalmed by definition. 'Blinded' falls on a surface read since the ships lay 'within sight of one another', 'not a spar broken' kills capsized, and reaching harbor kills beached.

P32.note: The final sentence is a three-kill list: 'sheds stood as before' (bombarded), 'no alliance warship came near' (blockaded) and 'flag went on flying' (annexed). Wool vanishing from the alliance's own markets while neutrals load more gives boycotted.

P33.note: 'The same nitrogen in the top foot' kills both leached and manured, with 'clear' water backing up manured. 'Hard, cracked plates' kills mulched. Planting held until the ground 'would at last bear a tractor's weight' gives mired.

P34.note: 'The survey's size' kills enlarged, 'north at the top of both' kills flipped, and 'as bare of ornament' kills gilded, all from one sentence. The channel moved across a reef at the navy's harbor, sold to foreign captains, gives doctored.

P35.note: 'Shoved forward into folds ... each a stride from the next' gives rippled. The stakes sentence lists the kills: roadbed 'at the height it was laid' (raised), the wheel tracks 'stayed level' (rutted) and 'nowhere did it crack' (ruptured). That stakes sentence is a comma splice and needs repair.

P36.note: 'Crept down the valley in every cold decade and drawn back in every warm one' alone gives thermometer. The meltwater sinking and low dry-summer flow kill storeroom (the water-tower trope), 'hardly changes between morning and night' kills timepiece, and the road 'miles below the ice' kills signpost.

P37.note: The cleaner-station picture and the parasite comparison give clinic; cleaner stations are widely known, which lowers difficulty. 'Ballroom' falls on a surface read because nothing in the passage is social or dance-like. 'Canteen' literally fits the shrimp that 'feed', and 'by day' with 'within minutes' kills bedroom.

P38.note: 'Walked slowly toward the elk' kills chased, and the open approach in a wide arc kills ambushed. 'By spring the elk were back grazing the benches' kills cowed. Driving the herd into a chest-deep side canyon gives corralled.

P39.note: 'Duties ... were paid later, at the customs house' kills tollbooth, the near-miss. 'Ships tied up to unload' at the piers kills wharf, and swells that 'rolled over the bar' kill seawall. Ships passing 'one behind another, each logged by name and hour' gives turnstile.

P40.note: A list with 'a sum written beneath the total', paid by the council's bankers before the crates come back, gives ransomed. 'Seals unbroken' and careful listing kill ransacked, return to the same museum kills repatriated (the planted carried-off history is the bait), and return on payment kills requisitioned.

tells: Three-kill template: in most items each wrong option is denied by its own planted 'as before / unchanged / no X' phrase, often stacked in one sentence, and the key is the one option left undenied, so a solver can eliminate without inferring. P03, P04, P06, P14, P19, P20, P21, P25, P27, P28, P32, P33, P34, P35, P38, P39, P40.

Counter-trope keys: the option matching the popular science story for the setup is the distractor, and the passage explicitly negates it, so 'pick the option the passage is at pains to deny is NOT the key' predicts the answer. Corridor in P02, greened in P14, reduced in P20, dislodged in P21, herded in P18, patrolled in P22, tomb in P16, banquet in P30, firebreak in P08.

Recycled frames across items: P12 and P27 (merchant ship carrying iron bars and wine, divers survey in 1990); P20 and P38 (wolves return to a mountain valley, elk herd); P18 and P22 (ants on a plant, then a 'her/the report concludes the ants had ___' blank).
Alliterative option sets with the key inside: P02 (c-), P09 (p- x3), P20 (r-), P22 (p-), P24 (c- x3), P35 (r-), P40 (r- x3). This is not predictive of the letter but is a visible authoring signature.

A trailing sentence after the blank often supplies the last kill or the confirming fact (for example 'In dry summers both valleys turn the same brown', 'Its benches stand mostly empty at midday', 'A gale ... left both halves standing'). P10, P13, P14, P18, P21, P33, P39.
